key_insight: RLVR can teach accurate step-by-step reasoning in-distribution yet fail under harder shifts by reverting to ineffective brute-force enumeration.
engineering_relevance: Training-task design can influence whether outcome-rewarded models retain effective reasoning strategies beyond their training distribution.
method: Use non-bijective string equations f(x)=y requiring multiple input solutions.
Test easy-to-hard shifts, including more solutions and longer outputs.
Co-train with bijective inversion tasks to reinforce derivation without process supervision.
evidence_signal: In the controlled equation-solving framework, OOD shifts caused sharp accuracy drops and strategy collapse, while bijective co-training substantially restored derivation and accuracy.
watch_item: Results come from a controlled string-equation setting; transfer to broader reasoning tasks remains unestablished.
paper_title: Not All Reasoning Generalizes: A Case Study on Learning Generalizable Reasoning Strategies in RLVR
